domain_test.declared_expectation: The protocol declared, before any number was seen, that a sound pair of methods would each win their own column. Whatever happened is reported as measured.
domain_test.question: Is each method better inside its own training domain than outside it?

gc_diagnostic.statement: Gate v12 recorded that this project's objective collapses to transcript GC at r = +0.99 on the synthetic design pool. Here, on 122 real measured constructs, the same objective correlates with GC at +0.7812, so the collapse is a property of the objective and not an artifact of the design pool's composition.

no_claim: Nothing here is a new measurement. Every label is from the source paper.

No claim about either method's translation side. RiboNN is not run here, and mRNAutilus's translation head is trained on Zheng et al. 2025, which is RiboNN's own training source, so that comparison would be partly circular.
No claim that either method resolves the narrow bin; chance is 0.50.
No resolution claim on mRNAutilus's arbitrary output scale.
No claim about mRNAutilus's generator. Only its half-life regressor was run.
Neither the source archive nor mRNAutilus's weights are redistributed here.
purpose: Compare this project's stability objective against mRNAutilus's half-life head on the SAME designed constructs, scored against BOTH in-solution and in-cell measured half-life, so that each method is tested inside and outside its own training domain.

source.not_redistributed: Only the URL and both hashes are pinned, as for the RiboNN weights, the Rfam sources and the mRNAutilus checkpoint. The archive and table are not copied into this repository.

the_free_baseline.statement: A free per-nucleotide EternaFold score, which requires no training and no calibration, is carried in both columns because the protocol declared it. On in-solution it reaches +0.4190 against this project's calibration at +0.3200. On in-cell it has the wrong sign. The calibration therefore does not beat free folding on its own home axis, which is the same finding the v10 ablation recorded and this test does nothing to relieve.

the_two_measured_axes_barely_agree.consequence_for_this_comparison: Winning one column implies nothing about the other. The earlier one-column comparison could not have been repaired by more in-solution data, which is what gate v13 recorded as a prohibition.
the_two_measured_axes_barely_agree.statement: In-solution and in-cell half-life of the SAME 122 constructs rank at Spearman +0.0545. They are very nearly unrelated orderings. This is the single most important number in this artifact: it means no predictor can rank both axes well, the two columns are separate tasks rather than two views of 'stability', and any method claiming to predict 'mRNA stability' must say which one it means.

what_this_changes: The axis question is settled: in-solution and in-cell stability are nearly unrelated on identical constructs, so 'stability' is not one target.
The earlier head-to-head is now correctly bounded. It measured one column of a two-column problem, and the column it measured is the one this project trained on.
The free-baseline problem is worse than previously recorded, not better: on in-solution, free EternaFold now ranks ABOVE the frozen calibration.
